title: Personality-first portfolio system: one concept across ten screens
attribution_visible_in_image: The name 'Robin' appears as the portfolio owner in the mockup. Not confirmed as the creator.
contains_third_party_content: Brand logos in a 'Trusted by' row (DJI, Formula 1, Nike, Honda, Porsche and others), stock-looking photos and 3D objects.

observed.layout: A grey board with a white grid holds ten desktop screens in a shared frame: lined-paper background, a slim nav of small colored pill tabs (HOME in yellow when active, ABOUT, CASE STUDY, PLAYGROUND, CONTACT) and colored dots. Hero: 'ROBIN' in a red selection box with handles, floating pastel stickers, 'I design software that gets out of your way.' with a green circle and pink asterisk inline, a black 'CONTACT ME' button. Playground: a collage of tilted, taped images and 3D objects. About (two screens): a handwriting-style bio, a taped polaroid, colored skill tags; a pixel-font 'ABOUT' with an outlined bio box. Featured works: pixel-font title and two project cards with date chips; then an angled black/yellow overlapping project layout with 'VIEW PROJECT'. Case study: pixel-font title, pastel metadata stickers (role, timeline, team), a large phone photo. Results: stickers with 47% and -55% beside two photos. Trusted by and Let's talk: logos on pastel tags, a smiley. Contact: a selection-framed 'CONTACT', a yellow sticky note, taped polaroids.
observed.hierarchy: One pixel headline per screen; the black button is the action.
observed.typography: Pixel display font, handwriting font and a plain sans. Typeface unconfirmed.
observed.materials: Paper lines, tape, sticky notes, pastel tags.

interpretation.aesthetic: Designer's desk meets design tool; warm, human, with a wink.
implementation_notes: Many rotated, layered items per screen; assets are images and CSS transforms.
Small token set repeated on every screen.
interpretation.caveat: Body text is unreadable at this resolution, so only large headings were measured.

concept_work.essence: A small token set (paper, tape, pastels, one pixel headline, one black button) applied to ten layouts so they read as one site.
what_makes_it_work: The selection-box device turns the name into a tool object, saying 'software designer'.
The board covers every portfolio section in a story order: hello, who, what, proof, trust, contact.
Sticker colors map to meaning (role, time, team, stats).
gaps_to_make_it_work: Body text cannot be read at this resolution, so its contrast and copy cannot be verified.
The handwriting font for bio text may hurt legibility.
Nav pills are tiny; many rotated and layered items risk clutter on small screens.
No states beyond the active tab.

shared_tokens: pixel plus handwriting plus sans type trio
links: The active nav pill is yellow on every screen.
Sticker colors map to meaning across screens (role, time, team, stats).

pattern.name: Personality-first portfolio system
use_when: Individual designers and studios with a human voice
adaptation_examples: Architect portfolio with blueprint paper and stamps.
Illustrator portfolio with a sketchbook metaphor.

lessons: One material metaphor repeated on every screen unifies different layouts.
Show every section of a portfolio in story order.
open_questions: Higher-resolution source to verify body text?

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: Lined-paper off-white ground, four pastels for stickers, black buttons, photos for color.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: The board shows a portfolio's full story and its purpose is obvious.
A strong, coherent look from a small token set.
Section order and conventions of a portfolio are followed; small body text could not be verified.
Only the active nav state is shown; interactions are not.
The same tokens are applied across ten screens.
The selection-box and desk metaphor are distinctive and serve the brand.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 16.07:1; secondary text min n/a:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
